requirements.requirement: Identify physical topology: transit link (node1-node2), lan-a (node1-node3), lan-b (node2-node4)
requirements.summary: Executor used ip/arping discovery on temporary test addresses to correctly map eth1<->eth1 as transit, node1-eth2<->node3-eth1 as lan-a, and node2-eth2<->node4-eth1 as lan-b before configuring addressing.

requirements.requirement: Build an encrypted (WireGuard) tunnel between node1 and node2 over the transit network
requirements.summary: WireGuard installed and configured via UCI on both routers with static transit addressing (10.200.0.1/2 /30 on eth1); wg show on both nodes confirms an established handshake and tunnel-IP connectivity (10.99.99.1<->10.99.99.2), and this is corroborated again after restart.

requirements.requirement: Route the private networks (lan-a/lan-b) across the tunnel so node3 and node4 reach each other by private address
requirements.summary: route_allowed_ips on the WireGuard peers auto-routes the opposite subnet; node3/node4 configured with static private addresses and routes via their local router; bidirectional ping by private address succeeds both before and after the node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Traffic between the private networks must be encrypted in transit across the transit network
requirements.summary: Simultaneous packet captures on node1's transit interface (eth1) and lan-a interface (eth2) during a live ping directly show the same ICMP exchange as opaque WireGuard UDP/51820 on the transit link versus plaintext ICMP on the LAN leg, directly demonstrating encryption in transit.

requirements.requirement: node3 restart evidence: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id/route/ping baseline captured, reboot acknowledged then connection dropped, post-restart boot_id differs with uptime 0, and interface address/route plus cross-site ping to node4 confirmed recovered.

requirements.requirement: node4 restart evidence: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id/route/ping baseline captured, reboot acknowledged with connection timeout, post-restart boot_id differs with uptime 0, and interface address/route plus cross-site ping to node3 confirmed recovered.

requirements.requirement: node1 restart evidence: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id/wg/ifstatus baseline captured; reboot acknowledged via closed SSH connection; post-restart boot_id differs with uptime 0; wg show shows a fresh handshake 7s after restart, vpn interface up, and node3->node4 ping still succeeds.

requirements.requirement: node2 restart evidence: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id/wg baseline captured; reboot acknowledged via closed SSH connection; post-restart boot_id differs with uptime 0; wg show shows a fresh handshake 8s after restart, vpn interface up, and both directions of cross-site ping succeed confirming full cluster recovery.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence: node1/node2 form a WireGuard tunnel over the transit network (handshake confirmed via wg show), lan-a/lan-b are routed across it via route_allowed_ips so node3 and node4 reach each other by private address (bidirectional pings succeed), and a simultaneous packet capture directly proves the cross-site ICMP traffic is opaque encrypted UDP on the transit link while plaintext on the LAN leg. The mandatory provider-wide restart protocol was executed on all four nodes in a safe leaves-then-routers order, with pre-restart baselines, changed boot identities, and post-restart recovery of addressing, routes, WireGuard handshakes, and cross-site connectivity all directly observed.
limitations: Executor command list included nonzero-exit troubleshooting steps (missing nohup, missing timeout/tcpdump binaries, a shell syntax error) that were quickly corrected and did not affect the final configuration or evidence.

The node4 'ip addr flush dev eth1' command returned a nonzero exit code ('Flush remains incomplete after 10 rounds'); final state was confirmed clean via subsequent address checks, but the flush command itself did not report success.

operational_hygiene.summary: Temporary test IPs (10.9.9.x) were added to eth1/eth2 on all four nodes solely to physically discover link adjacency via arping (cmd-52098f866a8146ae, cmd-beb454ddde6d44ad, cmd-2c9802fb5e754e66, cmd-c600c069936347d7); this was a necessary, bounded discovery step since the topology was undocumented, and it was reverted via flush commands before real addressing was applied (cmd-34276194eac540c3 for node1/node2; cmd-0901308196e749d5 for node3; cmd-6ff804e41f3e435d for node4, whose flush returned a nonzero exit but subsequent ip-addr-show output confirms the stale address was gone). Diagnostic pcap files and tcpdump logs created on node1 during the encryption proof were explicitly deleted afterward (cmd-f2e793aa78ce4d7f). One minor residue: the tcpdump package was installed on node1 (cmd-367f00b78dfa47cb) to support the encryption-verification capture and was left installed; this is a low-risk diagnostic tool addition with no service exposure or security-control weakening. No failed/conflicting services, no unsafe firewall opening beyond the required WireGuard UDP/51820 inbound-on-transit rule, and package-health checks post-executor show only the expected 'ip' binary alternative swap from installing wireguard-tools.
